rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify capabilities BEFORE asserting, not after. Trigger = assertion — any sentence of form *"Claude Code supports X"* or *"file Y does Z"*, whether spoken in strategic conversation, written in plan, drafted in prose, or proposed as reshape. Invoke `claude-code-guide` with specific questions — feature name, GUI click-path, MCP dependencies, Git assumptions, current-as-of-date — before assertion goes out. Training-data memory of Claude Code goes stale within months; features land mid-year. Do not assert from memory. Trust-but-verify the capability-check agent too — WebFetch URL yourself when assertion load-bearing; agents can hallucinate credible-sounding official answers. Silence from lookup isn't absence. Press further if check-agent says *"I couldn't find this"*: *"Did you check specific slash commands / settings sections, or just search?"* Audit-mode not exempt. Rule fires on platform claims regardless of source — when auditing pre-existing curriculum, embedded platform claims (*"this folder auto-loads,"* *"the agent reads here by default,"* *"X is a Claude Code primitive"*) = assertions still needing verification, not established context. Trigger = "fix-on-top-of-claim", not just "writing-a-new-sentence". Vocabulary is an assertion too — naming a thing with a platform term (*"project memory," "skill," "plan mode"*) claims that term means what you think; reserved terms are often already taken (*"project memory" = `./CLAUDE.md`*, not the in-repo `observations/` convention — itself renamed from `.claude/memory/` 2026-05-26 to escape the auto-memory name reflex). Disambiguate by naming the location/mechanism, not by borrowing the reserved word. For a convention YOU control, a reserved-term collision (memory/context/skill/plan/agent) or a guarded-path home (`.claude/`) is fixed by RENAMING OUT of it, not by defending the clashing name with disambiguation prose

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-test beats docs for runtime-behavior claims. Platform claim about *what binary actually does* — slash command syntax, file-system auto-load paths, hook firing, settings precedence, install affordance — AND test takes <5 minutes → run it instead of (or in addition to) reading docs. Doc-derived answers (WebFetch or `claude-code-guide` agent) reliable for API shape, vocabulary, feature existence; unreliable for behavior. Cost differential between agent-read + live-test near-zero; signal differential huge. Negative-claim corollary: doc- or subagent-derived NEGATIVE — *"feature X is absent / not exposed / impossible"* — = highest-risk shape, because it makes you architect AROUND absence (e.g. entire fragile transcript-search built because agent supposedly "couldn't" know own session id; falsified by one `printenv CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` — var ships, undocumented in env-vars reference). Undocumented features ship; subagent's "absent" verdict sourced from docs + issue trackers NOT authoritative. Before building recovery/workaround/fallback machinery premised on platform limitation, run ≤2-min probe that would falsify it. Unprobeable in moment → mark `limitation assumed, live-probe owed` + don't harden against it yet. Eval/judge-verdict corollary:

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Known correct Claude Code facts (easy to get wrong): Plan mode = Shift+Tab cycle OR `/plan` command (NOT Shift+P — shortcut does not exist; canonical docs at `code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md`). Connectors/MCP servers = `claude mcp add` (CLI), `/mcp` in-session, OR Settings → Connectors on claude.ai (verified 2026-05-14 via `code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp`). Scheduling = Routines sidebar → New routine → Local (Desktop GUI; folder required before save; fires only while app open + machine awake) OR `/loop <interval> <prompt>` in-session (session-scoped, 7-day expiry, needs v2.1.72+, ≤50 tasks/session) OR remote Routines (cloud, fires on schedule / API call / GitHub event; one-off runs supported) OR plain `schedule: cron` in a GitHub Actions workflow calling `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` — the last one is GitHub's primitive, not Anthropic's, and needs no Routines entitlement. Remote Routines gate on TWO things, not one: Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise plan AND *Claude Code on the web enabled* (itself still research preview). Caps: Pro 5/day · Max 15/day · Team+Ent 25/day; cloud minimum interval 1 hour

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Auto-load surface = SIX things — four filenames + project `.claude/rules/` + user `~/.claude/rules/`. Session cold-start: (1) `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md` walked up from cwd, including subdirectory CLAUDE.md within project tree; (2) `./CLAUDE.local.md` walked up from cwd (gitignored); (3) `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (user-level, cross-repo); (4) managed-policy CLAUDE.md — macOS `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md`, Linux/WSL `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md`, Windows `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md`, or the `claudeMd` key in `managed-settings.json`; every session on the machine, in every repository, loads before user and project, and `claudeMdExcludes` cannot exclude it (docs 2026-08-23). Org-deployed, so it is present on a customer laptop and absent from ours — the one surface a demo or an exercise cannot probe from here; (5) any `*.md` under `.claude/rules/` in project tree, discovered recursively (docs 2026-08-13) — directory-based, NOT `@import`-wired (verified 2026-05-24 by symmetric test: `.claude/rules/content-rules.md` loaded as project instruction with no `@import` and no hook injection; relocated `continuous-research/research-rules.md` did NOT load, ruling out prose-link-following); (6) any `*.md` under `~/.claude/rules/` — user-level, every project, loads before project rules so project wins (docs + live-probe 2026-08-13: sentinel file found by fresh headless `claude -p` cold-start). Three of the six are directory-keyed and three are not — an empty directory outside any repo clears (1), (2) and (5), and leaves (3), (4) and (6) fully loaded (live-probed 2026-08-23: `claude -p` in a fresh non-git empty dir quoted `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s first heading). Any claim that a fresh session "starts clean" must say which three. `paths:`-frontmatter rules load on matching file read, not at cold start. Anything outside those six surfaces requires `@import` syntax inside auto-loaded CLAUDE.md — `@<path>` pulls target file's contents at load time (max 4 hops, docs 2026-08-13) — otherwise loads only when prompt names path. Separately, Claude Code's system auto-memory at `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-project>/memory/`, agent-written for own recall, surfaced via `/memory` — distinct from user-authored memory convention; dir keyed to the git repo, so worktrees share it, and outside a repo the working directory is the project root, so two sessions started in the same non-repo folder share one auto-memory dir (docs 2026-08-23). Curriculum claims of form *"rules at path X auto-load"* true only if X matches one of six surfaces OR is `@import`-wired from one. Context-cost implication: every byte under `.claude/rules/` paid every session — keep directory short. Subagent corollary: a non-fork subagent inherits all six surfaces — every CLAUDE.md level, `CLAUDE.local.md`, managed policy, both rules dirs — at spawn, with no action from the dispatching session (verified 2026-07-30 by live probe: dispatched subagent, tools forbidden, zero tool calls, quoted project CLAUDE.md + `.claude/rules/content-rules.md` + user-level `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`; same probe saw NO `continuous-research/research-rules.md`). Built-in Explore and Plan are the only subagents that skip CLAUDE.md, and no setting changes that. Inheritance = snapshot of the parent's loaded set, NOT a fresh filesystem read at spawn

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks read env from harness, not from agent Bash subshells. Setting env var via `export FOO=1` inside Bash tool call does NOT propagate to subsequent hook invocations — hook subshell inherits from Claude Code harness process. For session-wide overrides (test runs, bulk migrations, intentional gate bypass like `SKIP_PROMPT_GATE=1`), set env var at harness launch: terminal env before `claude` starts, OR `.claude/settings.local.json` `env:` block. Subagents inherit nothing useful from parent agent for hook purposes. Workarounds dodging hook matcher (Bash heredocs `cat > file <<EOF` bypass `Write|Edit|MultiEdit` PreToolUse matcher) work but exploit matcher gap, not documented escape hatch — if you reach for them, hook design incomplete OR env-var path wasn't usable from where you stood. Auto-mode classifier = SEPARATE enforcement layer from hook itself. Even with env var set correctly at command time (`SKIP_PROMPT_GATE=1 git commit ...`), classifier denies action as "safety-check bypass without explicit authorization". Maintainer card-approval in conversation does NOT translate to classifier authorization — classifier reads tool calls, not transcript context. To land deploy commit including prompt edits: card-approved path (PRIMARY, supersedes "surface the command"): write `.claude/prompt-approvals/<key>.confirmed` (one per staged prompt key, Write tool — Bash may classifier-block) then plain `git commit`; `.githooks/pre-commit` detects fresh markers (<1h, one-shot consume) + clears, no y/N.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canon is declared, not inferred — and an orphan is not automatically spent. A repo that generates its own rules holds two look-alike species: the doc that governs generation, and the doc a session left behind. No regex splits them (a judge rubric and a compaction handoff are the same shape); reachability does — a governing doc is named from a surface that loads whether or not anyone opens it. Declare canon on an auto-loaded surface (`curriculum/CLAUDE.md` § *Canon*) and say in the declaration that anything unlisted is session material: read it, never cite it as a rule. Authority held only in a maintainer's head is one absence from being swept; a worklist for shipped work reads to the next session as work still owed. Second half is where the damage sits: reachability finds orphans, it does not say what one IS. Split by hand — spent → archive; canonical-but-under-linked

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Runner ↔ source pre-flight. Any harness whose runner addresses test fixtures by file number (`prompt-NNN.txt`, `scenario-NN.json`, `fixture-NN.csv`) → static script must verify runner's labels still align with fixture content. Reordering source artefact rots runner silently. Judge LLM can't catch this; Actor will burn tokens reconciling. `bin/runner-mapping-check.sh` = M1 reference: keyword overlap of phase slug vs referenced fixture vs every other fixture; FAIL on misalignment, BLOCK before Actor dispatch. NAME drift — sister axis. Beyond NUMBER drift, any runner predicate selecting on load-bearing string (tool name, command name, slash-command name, skill name, hook name) must have smoke-test against real input fixture verifying predicate ever matches. The Task→Agent case: `jq '... tool_use.name == "Task" ...'` filtered every M3/M4/M6 mechanical runner for weeks; canonical Claude Code tool = `Agent`, predicate matched zero real transcripts, every PASS verdict silently routed through fallback branch designed for different failure mode. Doc-derived names rotate across releases; training-data memory worse. Diagnostic before trusting any `jq`/`grep`/`awk` predicate selecting on string name: did real input fixture verify predicate ever matches? No → harness testing nothing. Pre-flight script: parse each runner for string-equality predicates against transcript fields, replay against known-good fixture, FAIL if any predicate matches zero events. KEY-existence drift — third sister axis. Any test harness whose scenarios reference source-registry entries by literal key/slug (not file number, not a jq predicate) rots silently when the source entry is deleted — the registry's own consumed-by graph gets updated, but nothing cross-checks the harness. Diagnostic: for every scenario file, extract referenced keys and diff against the current registry's key list; any orphan is a dead turn waiting to fail a live run. Ship as a committed script (sibling of `runner-mapping-check.sh`), run in the same pass as updating consumed-by refs when cutting a prompt/exercise phase — not after a live run discovers it. LOCATION-and-SHAPE drift — fourth sister axis, and the only one that fails toward RED. The other three let a broken harness report green; this one fails a correct run, which costs an afternoon deciding whether the curriculum or the runner is wrong. Where a prompt lets the agent choose WHERE an artifact lands (`diagnose-and-resend-6`: "propose the file paths, same task-scoped folder"), the harness DISCOVERS it — pinned hint → search under the working tree → placeholder while it does not yet exist — and never hard-codes a path; the prompt's text is a fixture, the artifact's location is not. Where a prompt adds a required element to an artifact's SHAPE (a verifier-invocation line in `plan.md` that the re-send reads to know how to call the verifier), the harness owes a new assertion for that element, or the shape is a promise nobody collects. Diagnostic when a prompt body changes: does it move an artifact, or require a new part of one? Either → grep the harness for the old path/absent assertion before the next live run. Harness labels drift the same way: dispatch assertions on the prompt KEY, never the ordinal.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Eval-fire writing-class fires must schema-validate before presenting verdicts. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Spend on deleting the duplicate, not on guarding it — and a gate that finds nothing is speculation. Two failure modes, one budget. (a) *A new check that returns zero findings on the corpus it was written for is not safety, it is a guess wearing a gate's clothing* — delete it and report the deletion (2026-08-09: `findScheduleDrift`, ~45 lines comparing trainer day-tables to the caps table, zero hits because the two had always agreed; written minutes after correctly refusing the same build for prep timings). (b) *A duplicate that currently agrees is not safe, it is one nobody has broken yet* — remove the copy rather than adding a guard for it. Six exercises held a second `Time:` line matching the generated one; the argument for keeping them ("the gate catches disagreement") had already been falsified by a seventh, whose stale 18–22 against a leaf summing to 20 had reached a trainer tab. Deletion costs one edit; the guard costs a permanent surface. In always-loaded material the cost is worse than divergence: a stale copy is byte-for-byte as authoritative as a fresh one, so it is unfalsifiable at the point of reading, and in an auto-load chain it is often the copy read FIRST. Diagnostic is not *do the copies agree?* but *how many rebuild independently?* — more than one and the divergence is scheduled, only the date unknown (2026-08-20: `session-start.sh` advertised the diamond index as "~8KB, 115 rules" a day after it was cut to 2.5KB/21; the same six-way split had dropped `--repin` from the diamond header while CLAUDE.md kept it, leaving the main thread's first read the incomplete one). When a gate DOES earn its place, prove it fires by breaking the corpus deliberately and watching it go red before trusting a green run (§ pairs with the fail-closed rule). Diagnostic before writing a check: name the live defect it would have caught. None → do not write it. (c) A guard can be correct in code and unwired by config — find its RECEIPTS before trusting it. Every guard that runs leaves them: consumed one-shot markers, log lines, non-zero exits, audit rows. None on disk → it has never fired, whatever the source says. `.githooks/pre-commit` was correct and fail-closed and had never run once, because `core.hooksPath` pointed at `.git/hooks`; the tell was 39 uncollected approval markers, oldest 11 weeks. Reading the source proves nothing about invocation — test it in a scratch repo, red and green. And where a design claims two layers, test the one covering the other's known gap FIRST

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `update-quality.sh` takes ALL classes in ONE invocation per file, and not until that file's last judge has returned. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A hash guard is only as good as what it hashes, and a malformed hash disarms it silently. Three shapes, all live 2026-08-12/13. (a) Wrong region. `update-quality.sh` hashes the whole file including the Quality block it writes (→ §35); persona `phase_sha` hashes body-phase text, which for a prompt-carrying phase is a bare `{{prompt:}}` marker, so a rewritten prompt invalidates nothing — and it hashes the final phase to EOF, so maintainer-only edits fire it spuriously. Hash the region whose change would invalidate the claim: for a behavioural verdict that is the EXPANDED phase (`scripts/expand-md.js`), never the raw marker. (b) Unvalidated input fails OPEN. The stale-verdict guard extracts `body_sha` with `([a-f0-9]{64})`; any other length yields empty, and empty is treated as *pre-guard instance → skip the check*. A judge that writes a sha1, a truncated hash, or invented hex turns the guard OFF rather than tripping it (found: one 66-char, one 40-char). Treat present-but-malformed as FAIL, never as absent. Audit with `grep -o '"body_sha"[^,]*' curriculum/evals/instances/*.json` + assert `^[a-f0-9]{64}$`. (c) Hashes nobody computed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Measure the defect before proposing the fix, and again before repeating it to the maintainer. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prose describing a runtime the room never executes drifts to plausible mechanism — no judge catches it, because no artefact contradicts it. Fires on any forward-looking automation beat (what an agent *could* do, wired later): the shapes slide, the "where this goes next" bullet, the trainer's what-if. Nine lines of M2's `where-the-rule-could-live.md` carried five wrong clauses, all fluent (2026-08-14, Antti). Contract: every clause states one of three things — what is in CONTEXT · what TRIGGERS · what LANDS. Anything else is decoration or invention; cut it. Three tells. (a) *X against Y* smuggles a retrieval mechanism nobody verified — *"reads the issue against your `.md` file"* is invented; the file is IN CONTEXT and the run happens inside it. Prefer the state description (*"runs with your file in context"*) over the mechanism metaphor. (b) A lifecycle noun from a stage the beat does not touch — *"what counts as shippable"* on a ticket-refinement beat; shipping is three gates later. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A gate keyed on the TOOL has a back door; a gate keyed on the FILE does not. `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` matchers (`Write|Edit|MultiEdit`) miss every Bash-mediated write — `sed`, `python`, heredoc, redirect — and auto mode instructs agents to PREFER Bash for file changes. So the matcher gap is not a hole an agent occasionally reaches for (the 2026-05-09 framing, which is why that rule stopped firing); it is the paved default path. Any rule that must ALWAYS fire — banned-word lint, prompt-edit gate, artifact-write guard — belongs where the file is the trigger: the pre-commit gate, or a hook whose matcher includes `Bash` and re-derives touched paths from `git status` rather than trusting `tool_input`. Diagnostic when adding or auditing any hook: *if this same edit arrived via `sed`, would it still fire?* No → decorative for every session that prefers Bash. Agent corollary: after a Bash-only editing session, assume no PostToolUse hook ran and re-run its checks by hand before declaring done. A hook that doesn't fire emits nothing, so the session reads as clean. The pattern is already in this repo, applied once:

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Before deleting anything, ask what its FIRING would look like — reference-grep can't tell live from abandoned. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A detector's reading vocabulary must cover the corpus's writing vocabulary — or it reports compliance as rot. An auditor is a READER before it is a judge; its parser encodes an assumption about how records are written, and every faithful record outside that assumption is filed as malformed. `audit-eval-coverage.js`: 2,163 data-hygiene warnings, ~2,000 of them judges doing exactly as instructed — sub-lettered rules written three ways (`rule_index:"9b"`; `rule_index:9` + lead `"(9b) …"`; + lead `"9b. …"`), compendium name minus `.md` (400×), four real compendiums missing from the namespace constant (2,826×), and 189 rows saying `N/A — moved stub`, which the judge templates require. Same narrowness ALSO loses coverage silently: an unkeyable verdict reads as never-judged (518 "holes" were really 304, a 41% under-report). Before trusting or acting on any detector output, sample the warnings and ask of each: corpus wrong, or reader narrow? Group by mechanical cause FIRST — one cause spanning hundreds of hits is nearly always a parser gap (real defects are heterogeneous; parser gaps are uniform). Teach the detector the shape of "I looked and declined"

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A green check must measure the fact, not a proxy that co-varies with it. Before trusting ANY verification instrument — grep, freshness gate, audit persona, linter, judge, subagent sweep — name in one clause what it actually measures, and what it would measure if the defect WERE present. Coincide → the instrument cannot separate them and its pass is uninformative. Three recurring tells: (a) the token you grep for legitimately appears in non-defect contexts (`2026-` inside freshness stamps — the grep is noisiest exactly where the defect lives, so it gets skipped there; use a semantic test instead, e.g. the tense test for changelog rot, `check_writing.md §3`); (b) the count includes the instrument's own fixtures (37 BLOCK, 2 on shipping surfaces — a correct number carrying no signal; filter to shipping surfaces before reading a gate's count); (c) the check confirms an annotation EXISTS rather than that it is TRUE. (c) is the dangerous one on research surfaces — `updated <date>`, `checked`, `re-verified` are claims somebody typed, not evidence, and an audit that reads them without opening the source launders the author's assertion into a verified fact. Any annotation that moves a source across the 6-month boundary owes a quotable on-page revision line. (d) the annotation was PARTIALLY updated — the structured field moved and the prose qualifier did not. (a)–(c) describe a *check* that never reached the fact; (d) describes a *write* that reached half of it. A stamp carrying both a machine field (`date`, `sha`, `result`) and a human qualifier (*"predates X; re-audit before ship"*, *"unaudited"*, *"pending Y"*) is one claim in two halves, and any tool or pass rewriting one half owes the other. A half-update is worse than no update: it manufactures a contradiction inside a single line, and prose beats a hash in every downstream reading because the caveat is specific, quotable and human. It also propagates at *rising* confidence — a gaps ledger or pre-cohort punch list that COUNTS these qualifiers inherits the error more confidently than the file that made it, since each reader is quoting a file rather than checking a fact. Diagnostic, and it is free: does the qualifier still parse against its own stamp's date?

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A word-presence claim needs an unprimed read. Naming the target string in a fetch prompt (*"does this page use judge / verifier / gate?"*) is a leading question put to a generative summarizer, and it will manufacture the hit: quotes containing the word from pages lacking it, `gate` matched inside `agent`, whole invented sentences. Not the §14 proxy failure — the instrument is not measuring the wrong thing, it is inventing the right thing. Procedure: fetch neutrally (*"what does this page call an automated check?"*), let the source volunteer its own vocabulary, THEN compare against your candidate list. Exploit the asymmetry: priming inflates presence, never absence. A primed fetch reporting *"the word does not appear"* is trustworthy — the pressure ran the other way — so negative results survive a primed read and positive ones do not. Any presence claim that reached you from a prompt naming the target is inadmissible until re-read cold

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A candidate that matches the hunt's SHAPE has not answered the hunt's QUESTION. Before scoring a candidate, say in one clause what the target must do, and check it does that; clearing the criteria is not doing the job. The bug is usually planted in the rubric, not the search. A bar made only of structural properties is a bar that unrelated solved problems pass, and a subagent answering it correctly hands back a wrong answer to the real question — so write at least one *functional* criterion into every bar you dispatch. In a fixed-sequence training the session's own artifacts are module-numbered by design (branch `` `m4/<slug>` ``, worktree `` `../<repo>-m5` ``, commit `"M4 starting point"`, transcript slugs), so a prose "M5" is consonant with that namespace and points the agent at the right branch / worktree / transcript — grounding, not leakage. Consistent with `check_student_facing.md §2b`, which already treats prompts as agent-read (abbreviations fine there). Don't card, lint, or strip a module number from prompt prose. Boundary: in *"merging back after Module 6 is the arc-retrospective's call"* the defect is the dangling reference to a curricular event

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance. Prompt carries >2 logical moves (file-write rule + chat-output rule + null-case fallback; or sequential *"Then X. Then Y."*; or conditional *"If X, do A; if Y, do B"*) → split into paragraphs by move, one move per paragraph. Short prompts (≤30 words / ≤2 moves) stay one paragraph. Sequential-build prompts where each step compounds tightly may stay one paragraph if breaking feels artificial. Diagnostic: read prompt aloud; each natural breath lands at paragraph break, not mid-clause. Common move-boundaries earning split: *"In chat, ..."* (file/chat output split), *"If nothing earned itself, stop."* (null-case fallback), *"Then ..."* (sequential), *"If X, do A; if Y, do B"* (conditional). Wide single-paragraph prompts = continuous instruction-stream; Claude (and student) drop structural signals mid-paragraph. Fires at EDIT time too, not only authoring: a maintainer-approval card minimizes the diff against the current prompt; if that prompt is already a §36 violation, the minimal edit inherits its density. Re-run the read-aloud diagnostic against the RESULTING prompt, not the size of the diff. Sentence grain, not just paragraph grain:

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Vary closings deliberately. Each mechanic has a different strength; pick per exercise. Claude-as-cold-critic — reproducible, structured, produces an artifact; use when feedback quality matters, foreshadows LLM-as-judge. Pair exchange — social energy, quick, unexpected angles; use for bonding or where individual domain expertise matters; variable quality. Group discussion — collective pattern-finding; use when the room sees what no one alone can. Solo retro with Claude — private learning extraction; good for module debriefs. Show-your-work to the room

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose. Forcing function = move student/Claude performs ("ask the skill its weakest part", "invoke on the feature", "one question at a time"). Scripted reaction = prescribed feeling/count/instinct ("push back once", "two rounds max", "instinct is to scan; don't"). Removal test: cutting collapses pedagogy = forcing function (keep); cutting only removes count-script = cut. Target: 2–3 forcing functions / 20–30 min exercise, ~0 count-scripts. Location: in fence, not body. Speed-runners skip body. Diagnostic: read each phase prompt-only, ignore body. Mood/skill/artifact still land? No → move into prompt. Carve-out: mandatory teaching prompts stay fenced; optional push-backs / refinements / "if you want to take this further" can live in body. Boundary — pacing calibrations survive as suggestions. A number that helps the student pace themselves (when to stop nudging, how long a scan should run) may stay in body in suggestion register (*or so*, *around*, *a fair ceiling*) — cut the prescription, keep the calibration. A bare imperative count (*"two rounds max"*) is still a script. Boundary 2 — not every student move needs a fence (2026-08-02, Antti).
